description: The phone's own host as a page: its name and whether it is in the mesh, the agents (Bots) that run on this phone, the models the mesh serves them, the phone's trash, and what the agents reach. Opened from the home screen's header; the phone's agents are also listed on the home screen under the host "phone".
opens: the "This phone" button (phone icon) in the home screen's header bar, left of Hosts
back from New Agent returns to it

parts.name: Bar
parts.shows: Title "This phone"; a back button at the start and a "New Agent" (+) button at the end.

parts.name: Phone card
parts.shows: The phone's name (its name in Android's settings, else its model's), a line saying whether it is in the mesh, and a paragraph: agents made here run on this phone (their chats, tools and files are here) and their models run on a machine of the mesh that serves them.
text: Not in the mesh: add a host first
Not in the mesh: none of your hosts is connected
Agents made here run on this phone: their chats, their tools and their files are here. Their models run on a machine of the mesh that serves them.

states.name: linked
states.shows: "In the mesh, through <host>" in the success colour

states.name: not linked
states.shows: "Not in the mesh" with the reason, or "add a host first" when no host is added; dimmed

parts.name: Agents
parts.shows: Heading "Agents", then a rounded list of this phone's agents that are not archived. Each row: the agent's picture (or initials), its name ("Agent" if it has none), its title or else its model's name, its status dot (with the asking mark when it asks something), and a trash button.

actions.does: opens the agent's chat (a chat on host "phone")
picks an image from the phone, shrinks it to a PNG 256 across at most and sets it as the Bot's picture
asks to move it to this phone's trash (below)

states.name: empty
states.shows: "No agents on this phone yet." and a New Agent button (the primary look when the mesh serves a model)

parts.name: Models
parts.shows: Heading "Models", a caption saying these are what the mesh's machines serve over an API (a model call goes through the mesh to the machine that has the model and runs there as that machine's own settings say), then a list with one row per provider and machine: "<provider> on <machine>" and the model names, two lines at most.
text: What the mesh's machines serve over an API. A model call goes through the mesh to the machine that has the model, and runs there as that machine's own settings say.

states.name: none served
states.shows: "No machine in reach serves a model over an API (Ollama, or an OpenAI-compatible server)."

parts.name: Trash
parts.shows: Shown only while the phone's trash holds an agent. Heading "Trash", then a row per trashed agent, newest first: its name and title (or model), and a Put Back button.

actions.does: restores its transcript, folder, picture and senders where they were and lists it again in Agents

parts.name: What they reach
parts.shows: Heading "What they reach" and a paragraph: files in each agent's own folder on this phone, questions to you, and the mesh's hosts and chats through this phone's connections to them; nothing else of the phone's; what it asks first is as its permission mode says, as in Baude.
text: Files in each agent's own folder on this phone; questions to you; and the mesh's hosts and chats, through this phone's connections to them. Nothing else of the phone's. What it asks you first is as its permission mode says, as in Baude.

parts.name: Move to trash dialog
parts.shows: Opened by an agent's trash button. Title "Move “<name>” to the trash?" (name: the Bot's, else "this session"); body: its transcript, its memory and the files in its folder will be moved to this phone's trash, where you can restore it. Buttons Cancel and Move to Trash (destructive).
text: Its transcript, its memory and the files in its folder will be moved to this phone's trash, where you can restore it.

actions.does: asks the phone's host to delete the session, which moves its files to phone/trash

parts.name: Chats with a phone agent
parts.shows: Its sessions are listed on the home screen under the host "phone" like any host's and open as an ordinary chat; the host's own name is the phone's. They differ from a chat on another host: the agent's loop and tools run on this phone, in its own folder; its model calls go through the mesh to a machine that serves the model, so only models the mesh serves can be picked, and none served means it cannot start; there is no connection banner for the host since it is the app itself; going back to an earlier message (rewind) is not supported; and a Bot's globe button is shown as in any Bot chat (PhoneUse.page.json).
text: an agent on this phone can't be taken back to an earlier message yet

states.name: no mesh
states.shows: The Models list says none is served and New Agent cannot be made until a machine serves one
